title: Participant state
description: What the server tells a device about its own participant. The mirror image of the observation envelope: observations flow up carrying a `schema_uri` and an opaque payload, and state flows down carrying a `state_uri` and an opaque state document. `epidemica_core` validates and caches this without ever learning what a particular study's state means, which is what keeps one study's vocabulary out of the platform. Scoped to the bearer token's own participant; a device can never read another's.

state_version.description: Selects the envelope this document is read as. A client that does not know this version must refuse it rather than interpret the parts it recognises.

subject.description: The pseudonym this state belongs to. Present so a cached document cannot be shown to the wrong participant after a re-enrollment on the same device.

state_uri.description: Absolute, immutable URI of the contract governing `state`. Dereferences to a JSON Schema, exactly as `schema_uri` does for an observation payload.

revision.description: Increases every time the server changes this participant's state. Lets a client tell a stale cached document from a current one without comparing timestamps, and lets it ignore a reordered response.

as_of.description: When the computation that produced this state ran -- not when it was served. A study whose state is recomputed daily is a day stale by design, and the interface should be able to say so rather than implying the number is live.

state.description: Study-defined content, validated separately against `state_uri`. Opaque to core, as an observation payload is.
